title: introduce-prefill-recipes-and-costchef-linter-for-automated-defaults
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for safe, opinionated defaults for batching, caching and quantization tailored to common workload archetypes. Ad-hoc defaults have drifted across components; operators end up copying heuristics into tenant configs. This PR introduces a small, auditable DSL ("recipes") and an accompanying CLI linter 'costchef' to generate, validate, and suggest tenant-level prefill/batching/caching/quant defaults.

What this PR does: - Adds a recipes schema and canonical set of three starter recipes (conversational-light, high-throughput-short, embedding-batch). Recipes encode: preferred batch shapes, kv-cache windowing, warmup prefills, quantization profile hints (int8/int4-fallbacks), and safe rollback thresholds. - Implements a lightweight server-side resolver that maps tenant workload tags to a chosen recipe and emits enforcement suggestions through the routing layer (no automatic enforcement in this PR). - Adds costchef CLI: validate <recipe>, diff <tenant-config> <recipe>, suggest <tenant-id> --dry-run. The CLI also runs an econ-linter that flags recipe constructs likely to increase unit-cost without latency benefit (e.g. large batch windows for sub-20 token median). - Adds unit tests, integration tests for the resolver, and a docs page with examples and migration notes.

Design notes and safety: Recipes are intentionally conservative: every hint has an associated fallback and a stability score. The resolver uses a deterministic scoring function (tenant usage histogram vs recipe signature) so suggestions are reproducible. This PR takes the conservative path: suggestions are emitted as config proposals and telemetry only; applying them requires an operator action (future PRs will add canary rollouts).

Checklist: - [x] schema, starter recipes, and recipe loader - [x] resolver & mapping logic - [x] costchef CLI + lint rules - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs page and example cURLs - [x] changelog entry + release notes

Related: ENG-4231 (prefill defaults project), SUP-1298 (tenant asking for automated suggestions). For usage examples see docs/prefill-recipes.md and the CLI help.

Notes for reviewers: the key behavioral change is the resolver suggestion stream; the serving runtime is not altered in this PR. I focused on test coverage for the default heuristics; please pay attention to the econ-linter thresholds (src/cli/costchef/lint_rules.py) and the mapping function in optimizer/recipe_resolver.py.

Operational impact: ships as a non-breaking addition. No database migrations. The resolver reads recipes from the same config bucket used for tenant defaults. Backwards-compatible: if no recipe matches, behavior is unchanged.
commits: feat(recipes): add recipe schema and starter recipes
feat(resolver): deterministic tenant->recipe matcher and suggestion emitter
test: add unit and integration tests for resolver and CLI
chore: wire recipe loader to config bucket and add telemetry labels
review_comments: Daniel Morales (2025-08-11): Nice direction — two asks: 1) can we add a simple perf-smoke that measures median p95 token latency for the three starter recipes on a small model so we can ensure no regression? 2) Move the econ thresholds into a single config file so SRE can tune them without code changes.

Aisha Patel (2025-08-11): Reply: added a small perf-smoke under tests/perf/test_recipe_smoke.py and factored lint thresholds into optimizer/recipes/lint_thresholds.yaml; CI will run the smoke in a gated job. See latest commit.

Priya Shah (2025-08-13): Suggestion: the CLI 'suggest' output should include estimated delta in token-cost per 100k requests for the tenant to make operator decisions easier. Can we surface a ballpark estimate?

Aisha Patel (2025-08-13): Reply: added a best-effort cost delta estimator that uses tenant token histogram + unit price heuristics. It's in costchef --dry-run and shows estimated savings and confidence score.

Ethan Liu (2025-08-14): Minor: docs examples show 'int4' as a safe default for embed_batch; please add explicit fallback to int8 when model not validated for int4. Also add a note about audit logs for recipe application.
Aisha Patel (2025-08-14): Reply: updated embed_batch.yaml to include quant_fallback: int8 and added audit notes in docs.
Daniel Morales (2025-08-15): Approve after CI green and one nit on log verbosity in resolver (suggest reducing DEBUG lines).
ci_checks: perf-smoke: pass (median p95 within 3% of baseline)
release_notes: Added 'recipes' as a first-class, auditable mechanism for tenant prefill/batching/caching/quant defaults. Introduced costchef CLI for validation, diffing and dry-run suggestions. Suggestions are proposals only; no automatic rollout. Includes 3 starter recipes and an econ-linter to flag risky defaults.
